title: THE WHALE THAT SWALLOWED THE EXIT
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: Widens the day's scale to inter-universal without leaving the body: the counterpart is a living stranger whose pain is physical, whose perspective (every transit wound feels like a harpoon, because previous universes mined its passages) is coherent and hard, and who cannot tell a refugee craft from an extraction swarm. This is the nonverbal encounter R14 explicitly allows, and the thirty-seven-hour collapse gives a clock that punishes force. The decisive idea (read gravitational rhythm as touch, turn a fixed wound into a paced migration whose timing belongs to the body bearing the cost) is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards, and love is an act of attention: she stays small enough to be felt, carries one family's song, and lets Uluun stop the first convoy. Everyone keeps a refusal: Uluun can stop each pulse, cities choose convoy order, families may take lifeboats.

First draft of S2 from selected candidate C06, following the B01 selection reason and biggest risk. B01 risk handled as follows: the cosmic scale is held by one family (Ysa, Dunya), one delegate who distrusts her (Corvane) and one dockhand dissenter (Marro Tell), five speaking roles in all; Uluun is never given speech and appears only through felt signal, rhythm and scar; the pulse insight is earned by visible work, not briefed: Illuminara notices the flinch comes before the cut (the forty-cycle cutter hum), reads the scar chart for the eleven marks that do not fit (clean, all on the crest), and then a small costed test, the Lark, shows the wall carries a quiet hum-singing ship for four hundred metres and throws it the instant the thrusters fire. Illuminara's smallness is the felt moment (less than a nerve ending, held up by water, 'like being allowed'), not pain or sacrifice. She refuses force at the decisive turn: she lets Uluun stop the first pulse for eleven minutes and does not use her power. Outcome (rule 3a): six billion people and every city escape; the rim-drift lifeboats give the dissenters a real alternative and Marro Tell a voice and a promise that the next plan begins with the boats; Uluun keeps a scar but chooses its own route and is tended by volunteer scar crews. Remaining costs: the Calyx and its stars are lost, the Lark is destroyed, eleven were injured, and the sanctuary must walk for generations. R14 observation: the turning point is the rehearsed, unamplified hum offered before any hull carries it (consent by rehearsal) and the unforced pause; what still needs checking is whether the Slack and Ocean scenes read as dramatised rather than explained, and whether Corvane's last line carries enough weight.

A strong, readable first draft with one genuinely good engine and several unearned joints. The good engine: the forty-cycle cutter hum is planted in scene 1 (the wall flinches before the arms touch it), the scar chart in scene 2 yields eleven clean marks all on the crest, and the Lark's costly failure in scene 3 teaches two things (when to touch, what the touch must sound like). That is intelligence shown by noticing, not announced. She also declines force at the decisive moment (the eleven-minute stop). What does not yet hold: (1) the hinge scene, the Ocean, is told in summary and rests on an unplanted 'other universes' wound and a first contact the wall never agreed to; (2) the success of a forty-kilometre crossing by six billion people is not shown to solve the very failure the Lark suffered at four hundred metres, so the evacuation ultimately depends on the wall's goodwill rather than on a worked-out method; (3) the strongest objector, Corvane, changes sides off the page and is then standing in the wrong place; (4) several numbers and a closing phrase do not close. Length is 2,771 words, above the normal range.

AUTHOR_REVISION answering the self-review CRITIC_REVIEW T02 (independent_peer_review=false). Kept per the review's protect list: the planted forty-cycle clue and the eleven clean scars, Ysa's guess with a hull attached, the costed failed crossing and 'That is mine to carry, not yours', the hum rehearsed once alone, 'a maybe' and 'like being allowed', Uluun's silence and right to stop, Illuminara's refusal to fire the drives, and Marro Tell's dissent with 'The next plan begins with you.' Outcome (rule 3a): six billion people and every city cross the Seam; the rim boats give the dissenters a real route; Uluun keeps its scar but chooses its own course and is tended by ten thousand volunteers; costs that remain are the lost Calyx and stars, the Lark, eleven injured, generations of scar work, and Marro Tell's displeasure. Decisive contributions of Illuminara: noticing the flinch precedes the cut, reading the eleven clean scars, commissioning the costed Lark test, making a withdrawable offer and reading what the wall leaned toward, designing the pacer, handing the call to the pilot, and declining to use force at the stop. Speaking roles: Illuminara, Dunya, Ysa, Hale Corvane, Marro Tell (five).

T03 repaired what T02 named: the first contact is now refusable and played (terms agreed, flinch, withdrawal, fifty-minute wait, second smaller offer), the lean has one controllable handle (where the hum sits), Corvane has a cost-bearing beat and a condition, Dunya holds the call, Marro Tell's boats are seen in the first pulse, and the clock is mostly closed. The result passes rule 3a. What remains is bounded, not structural: (1) the pacer is presented as the method that answers the Lark's failure, but the text never says why a hum in the middle holds the city off the edge when Ysa's hum aboard the Lark did not; (2) length went up (about 3,000 words by the worker counter, against a normal 1,500-2,500, and T02 asked for about 2,500), and two numbers still do not close ('a hundred million people' on the lead deck against six billion in three pulses; 'where the cities take six' with no unit); (3) the title promises a whale that never appears, and the three echo-less blanks planted in two scenes are never paid or acknowledged again.

AUTHOR_FINAL answering the self-review CRITIC_REVIEW T04 (independent_peer_review=false on that review). Kept per its protect list: the planted forty-cycle clue and eleven clean scars; the refusable first contact (terms, flinch, withdrawal, fifty-minute wait, second smaller offer); the costed failed crossing and 'That is mine to carry, not yours'; Uluun's silence and its right to stop each pulse; Dunya's call and the wait; Illuminara's refusal to fire the drives; Corvane's 'last to believe you'; Marro Tell's dissent and 'The next plan begins with you.' Outcome (rule 3a): six billion people and about four hundred cities cross the Seam; the rim boats give the dissenters a real route and the last word; Uluun keeps its scar, chooses its own course and is tended by ten thousand volunteers; costs that remain are the Calyx and its stars, the Lark, eleven injured, generations of scar work, and Marro Tell's displeasure. Decisive contributions of Illuminara: noticing that the flinch precedes the cut, reading the eleven clean scars, commissioning the costed Lark test, making a withdrawable offer and reading what the wall leaned toward, designing the pacer and understanding why the Lark's hum failed, handing the call to the pilot, and declining to use force at the stop. R14 observation: understanding and love become action in the Ocean (a refusable offer that reads what the wall leans toward, and leaving the three blanks alone) and at the thirty-first minute (the wait the pilot calls); power is offered and refused three times (the doorframe held 'politely', the drives, the lift) and the decisive turn is not power. Speaking roles: Illuminara, Dunya, Ysa, Hale Corvane, Marro Tell (five), each serving a choice or consequence.

T05 answers all three priority points of the T04 self-review. P1: the difference between the Lark and the pacer is now perceived rather than asserted: in the Ocean the lean slides to the swell's rim when the hum breaks and follows the hum when it is set low, aside or at the centre; Illuminara concludes that Ysa's hum rode inside the thing being carried, so the middle wandered with the hull, whereas a hum set ahead on the centreline is a middle that does not move; Corvane asks 'The Lark hummed too, Illuminara. What makes your skiff different?' in the council and gets a two-sentence answer, and at the eighth minute of the first pulse the set toward the port edge has a visible cause (the pacer drifted a hull-length) and a visible correction (the pilots shift their note). P2: the head-count now closes (about two billion per pulse, three pulses, six billion; 133 cities in the first pulse of about 400; rim drift thirty hours against six hours for the cities, with units), and the exposition was trimmed, though length remains about 2,900 words by the worker counter, above the usual range (acknowledged openly in the T05 response). P3: the whale is planted and paid (the harbor children's name, 'surfaced and took a door into itself and kept it', 'The whale was giving back the time it had taken') and the three echo-less blanks are twice acknowledged and left unexplained ('not hers to open'; Ysa looks a long time and says nothing). final_critic_line: Illuminara learns that a wounded living wall flinches before the blade, offers it a refusable hum, hands the call to the pilot who may wait, and six billion people cross a collapsing cosmos behind a dead-engined skiff while the wall keeps its scar and its own course.
